READABILITY.evidence: Names are clear (compile_json_path_final_key, HasKeyOrArrayIndex, rhs_json_path) and both new pieces have short comments explaining intent. Formatting matches the surrounding json.py code.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: Adds an overridable hook and reuses compile_json_path for the leading segments. A small subclass serves the internal array-index callers. No duplicated SQL, no per-backend copies, no dead code; the temp test file was removed.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: No error-handling paths were introduced. json.dumps(str(key_transform)) always quotes the final key, so an int rhs (has_key=1111) also becomes the object key "1111". That is slightly more defensive than the reference. No magic constants.

C7-07-CASE1.evidence: Only the final has_key key is treated as an object key, in the shared HasKeyLookup.as_sql used by SQLite, MySQL and Oracle. KeyTransformIsNull (sqlite/oracle) and KeyTransformExact.as_oracle now use HasKeyOrArrayIndex, so value__arr__1__isnull still addresses array elements. Intermediate segments are unchanged.
